result:
I found 10 rules whose behaviour didn't match their docstring (or the module docstring's shared rules), and fixed all of them in `pricebook.py`. I then checked all 150 rules against a reference built from their docstrings. The test covered quantities around each threshold, several unit prices and the error on negative inputs, and every rule now matches.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 13, 91, 138 | Used `round(...)`, which rounds the discount instead of flooring it | Changed to `// 100` |
| 14, 33 | Cap only applied when the discount was over 200,000 won (`min(disc, 100000) if disc > 200000 else disc`) | Always capped at 100,000 won |
| 21 | Cap was applied to the discounted amount before the percentage was taken, not to the discount itself | Discount is calculated first, then capped at 10,000 won |
| 35 | Used 4% instead of the documented 3% | Changed to 3% |
| 111 | Started at 21 units (`qty > 20`) instead of "20+ units" | Changed to `qty >= 20` |
| 115 | Used 16% instead of 15% | Changed to 15% |
| 137 | Used 9% instead of 8% | Changed to 8% |

Three places look different from the rest but give the same results, so I left them alone:
- **Rule 72** uses `qty > 10`, but it's a "marginal" rule, so the discount at exactly 10 units is 0 either way.
- **Rules 105 and 120** cap with `if disc > cap` instead of `min()`, which has the same effect.

STATUS: DONE
